deviations.description: scores of the training samples: 1.6.1 over all samples vs v2 over the training samples
deviations.explanation: 1.6.1 runs GSVA once over every sample before splitting; v2 fits the featurizer on the training samples of each fold, so a score depends on the cohort it was computed with (plan 4.4).
deviations.name: pathways_fold

findings: 1.6.1 computes the GSVA pathway scores once, over every sample of the dataset, in `create_precily_pathway_features` and the model reads the CSV; v2 fits the `pathways` featurizer on the training samples of each fold and scores unseen samples together with them. The scores of one sample therefore depend on the cohort (deviation `pathways_fold`).

Both sides call `gseapy.gsva` with the same options (Gaussian kernel, min_size=5, max_size=2000, mx_diff, threads=4, seed=42) and pivot the long result the same way, so a fit over the same samples gives the same scores (`pathways_all`). The 1.6.1 flow log2(TPM+1)-transforms the expression for TPM datasets before this call; v2 reads the `gene_expression` view as it is, so the case feeds both the same log-scale matrix.

On this random case the per-fold scores of the training samples differ from the once-over-all scores by up to 0.2 (Pearson 0.975, 12 pathways, 24 of 30 samples); the size depends on the cohort and is not bounded by a tolerance class, so the step is a deviation and misses `statistical`.
The v2 featurizer downloads the MSigDB C2 CP v6.1 file when the dataset has no `pathways_gmt`; this case supplies a small GMT in `uns` so that it stays offline.
